title: Multi-image-as-one-order grouping toggle (2-3 screenshots -> one multimodal call)
goal: Let a scrolled q-commerce order that doesn't fit one screenshot be captured as 2-3 images grouped into a SINGLE receipt and a SINGLE multimodal LLM call, so it produces one set of line items instead of N separate receipts each claiming the full order (working spec F2: 'without this an order becomes three receipts with triple-counted items').
in_scope: app/add/capture.tsx: a 'These are screenshots of one order (2-3 images)' checkbox toggle. When on, file selection/drop is validated client-side to exactly 2-3 files, ALL resolving (after existing HEIC->JPEG preprocessing) to an image extension (jpg/jpeg/png/webp) -- violating either shows an inline error and does NOT submit; it never silently falls back to the N-receipts path. When on and valid, calls a new uploadGroupedReceiptAction instead of the existing per-file uploadReceiptsAction; when off, behavior is byte-for-byte unchanged from today.

app/add/actions.ts: uploadGroupedReceiptAction(formData) -- same server-side re-validation posture as uploadReceiptsAction (never trusts the client toggle alone): re-checks 2-3 files, all accepted image extensions. Computes contentHash = hashFileBytes(Buffer.concat of each file's bytes, in the exact selected order) -- a single combined hash, deliberately NOT a set of independent per-file hashes. Checks findDuplicateReceipt(contentHash) once (same helper, no new dedup logic). On no duplicate: calls a new uploadGroupedReceiptFiles() (see next item), creates exactly ONE ingest_jobs row via createIngestJob(id), runs extraction once via after(() => runExtraction(id)). Returns UploadResult[] with exactly one element (reuses the existing UploadResult type/shape so capture.tsx's results rendering needs no branching).

lib/receipts/storage.ts: uploadGroupedReceiptFiles(files: {bytes: ArrayBuffer; ext: AcceptedExtension}[], contentHash: string) -> {id, storagePaths}. Uploads each file to its own path under the same household prefix, in order; inserts ONE receipts row with storage_paths = the ordered path array and mime = contentTypeFor(the first file's ext) (all grouped files share the same image family). On ANY step failing after one or more Storage uploads have already succeeded, removes ALL storage objects uploaded so far for this call before rethrowing -- extends uploadReceiptFile's existing single-object no-orphans cleanup to the plural case (dedup.ts's stated invariant: 'a rejected duplicate must not leave orphaned Storage objects or partial rows' applies identically to a failed grouped upload).

lib/llm/extract.ts: runExtraction downloads bytes for EVERY entry in receipt.storage_paths (previously only storage_paths[0] -- this is a strict superset for the existing single-file case, zero behavior change there). routeExtraction takes the full ordered byte list; when the receipt's mime is an image type and there is more than one path, builds one `{type:'image',...}` part per page in order (not just the first), preceded by an ADDITIONAL instruction appended ONLY when storage_paths.length > 1: 'These images are multiple pages/screenshots of the SAME single order -- do not count an item more than once if it appears in more than one image due to scroll overlap.' The shared EXTRACTION_PROMPT text itself is left unmodified for the single-file case (advisor-flagged: appending this unconditionally would pollute every ordinary single-screenshot parse for no reason). parse_path is 'multimodal' for the grouped case (matches the existing single-image branch's classification).

lib/review/data.ts + review-detail.tsx: left preview pane renders EVERY storage_paths entry (previously only the first) as stacked images in order when mime is an image type, so a human reviewer can see all grouped pages, not just page 1 -- getDocumentPreviewUrl called once per path (2-3 short-TTL signed URLs, negligible cost).
out_of_scope: Grouping PDF/HTML/MHTML/text files -- toggle is image-extension-only; a q-commerce order confirmation that's already a single PDF/email doesn't need grouping.

Cross-detecting the same 2-3 screenshots re-uploaded individually (ungrouped) as duplicates of a previously-grouped receipt, or vice versa -- content_hash is a hash of the specific ordered file set selected in ONE upload action; this is a deliberate, documented limit (dedup only catches an identical re-submission of the same grouping choice), not an oversight.
More than 3 images per group, or a mixed image+PDF group -- rejected client- and server-side, no partial/best-effort grouping behavior.
acceptance: Three screenshots grouped as one order produce a single receipt with no triple-counted items (A24). Split for testability: deterministic half (verified directly) -- one receipts row with 3 ordered storage_paths, one ingest_jobs row, one receipt_lines set, parse_path='multimodal'. LLM-dependent half (verified against a real extraction run, not assumed) -- the combined line set does not show each item 3x; checkExtractionQuality's existing >5% line-total-vs-order_total deviation check is a partial structural guard here too (working as designed, it would already flag gross triple-counting and trigger the Pro escalation retry), cited as a secondary safety net, not the primary proof.
invariants: A grouped upload always produces exactly one receipts row and one ingest_jobs row for the whole set, never one per image.

A failed grouped upload leaves zero orphaned Storage objects and zero partial receipts rows -- extends the existing single-file invariant from lib/receipts/storage.ts/dedup.ts to the multi-file case explicitly, not by assumption.
The anti-double-count LLM instruction is only ever appended when storage_paths.length > 1; the single-image and non-image extraction paths are byte-identical to their pre-S-25 behavior.

Toggle validation (2-3 images) is enforced independently client-side AND server-side; the server never trusts the client's file count or extension claims alone (matches the existing extension re-validation posture in uploadReceiptsAction).
